claims.text: The Pulumi `protect` resource option is a Pulumi-engine construct enforced entirely within Pulumi.
The Pulumi `protect` resource option is never sent to the cloud provider.
GCP Cloud SQL instances have a `deletionProtection` attribute that the cloud provider enforces independently of Pulumi.
AWS RDS instances have a `deletionProtection` attribute that the cloud provider enforces independently of Pulumi.
A resource can be unprotected in Pulumi and still refuse to delete due to provider-side deletion protection, or be protected in Pulumi while the provider allows deletion.

The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/ has a section 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' explaining how to tell Pulumi protect and provider deletion protection apart and resolve each.
Many cloud resources carry their own deletion-protection attributes that the provider or the cloud API enforces independently of Pulumi's `protect` resource option.
`deletionProtection` is a deletion-protection attribute on a GCP Cloud SQL instance.
`deletionProtection` is a deletion-protection attribute on an AWS RDS instance.
Pulumi's `protect` option and a resource's own deletion-protection attributes are complementary layers rather than substitutes for one another.

The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/ has a section 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' explaining how to tell the two protection layers apart and resolve a destroy failure caused by either.
Pulumi's `protect` resource option is an engine-level guard that never reaches the cloud provider.
The page /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/protect/ exists and explains how to remove the `protect` option.

Some Pulumi providers refuse to issue the delete call when a resource has a deletion-protection attribute, e.g. `deletionProtection` on `gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` and `gcp.container.Cluster`; the failure surfaces from the provider before any request reaches the cloud API.
AWS RDS `deletionProtection`, EC2 `disableApiTermination`, and Azure Resource Manager management locks are enforced by the cloud API, which rejects the delete call independent of Pulumi.
Azure management lock delete failures often return an error code such as `ScopeLocked`.
`pulumi destroy` deletes what is recorded in the stack's state, not what the program currently says, so setting the attribute to false in the program alone is not enough.

Remediation for provider- and cloud-enforced deletion protection: set the attribute to false in the program, run `pulumi up` so the change reaches the live resource and state, then run `pulumi destroy`.
If protection was already disabled outside Pulumi, `pulumi refresh` synchronizes state with reality and `pulumi destroy` then succeeds without an intervening `pulumi up`.
`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` has a provider-enforced `deletionProtection` attribute, and nested `settings.deletionProtectionEnabled` also guards the instance at the GCP API level.
`gcp.container.Cluster` has a provider-enforced `deletionProtection` attribute.
`gcp.bigquery.Table` has a provider-enforced `deletionProtection` attribute.
Destroying a `gcp.bigquery.Dataset` that still contains tables fails unless `deleteContentsOnDestroy` is true.
`aws.rds.Instance` and `aws.rds.Cluster` `deletionProtection` is enforced by the AWS API and defaults to false.
`aws.s3.BucketV2` `forceDestroy` defaults to false, and a non-empty bucket otherwise fails to delete.
`aws.ec2.Instance` `disableApiTermination` is enforced by the AWS API (EC2 termination protection).
`aws.dynamodb.Table` `deletionProtectionEnabled` is enforced by the AWS API and defaults to false.

`azure-native.authorization.ManagementLockByScope` and scope-specific variants such as `ManagementLockAtResourceLevel` exist; Azure Resource Manager enforces locks, and a `CanNotDelete` lock must be removed before the resource can be deleted.

Destroying an `azure-native.keyvault.Vault` only soft-deletes it; recreating a vault with the same name fails with `VaultAlreadyExists` until the soft-deleted vault is purged or recovered, and purge protection prevents purging until its retention period elapses.
